Reference / numbers/bigint

numbers/bigint#

An explicit integer wrapper with validated decimal parsing and numeric algorithms.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let count = BigInt("18446744073709551616");
let seven = BigInt(7);
count.sign();                  // 1
count.bits();                  // 65
count.string();                // canonical decimal
count.int();                   // the same number as an int

Description#

An explicit integer wrapper with validated decimal parsing and numeric algorithms. Ordinary std integer quantities use int directly (#511).

Okkama's int is already of any size, so a BigInt holds an int (#189): arithmetic is the int's, and digits are written only when string() asks. From text, construction accepts an optional minus followed by decimal digits. It never trims whitespace or accepts +; leading zeroes are normalized.

Arithmetic is the operators (#215) and the same names as methods (#190): a + b or a.plus(b), a - b or a.minus(b), a * b or a.times(b), a / b or a.divided(b), a % b or a.remainder(b), -a, and <, <=, >, >=. Division truncates toward zero (unlike int, whose / gives a rat); the remainder has the dividend's sign; both throw BigDivisionByZero. gcd/lcm are non-negative; gcd(0,0)=0 and lcm(0,n)=0.

let quotient = count / BigInt(3);
BigInt(2).power(100, 101);

power() requires exponent >= 0 and a positive result bit budget (1048576 by default). 0^0 is 1. An oversized result throws BigPowerLimitExceeded; impossible budgets are rejected before heavy exponentiation. This bounds result bits, not all backend memory or wall-clock time.

An integer of any size; it holds an int, so arithmetic is exact and fast.

object BoundedPower#

object BoundedPower

An exact int power with an explicit result-bit budget. BigInt.power and untrusted std parsers share this operation; no oversized product is made.

BoundedPower(base: 10).int(100, 4096);

Binds the base; int() validates the exponent and bit budget.

base^exponent, at most maximum_bits bits; 0^0 is 1.
